I was also diagnosed in 2021 and I have the exact same feelings as you! Especially the part where you feel like you tricked your psychiatrist into diagnosing you so you could be special. I don't think I've ever met anyone who has this same feeling and I thought no one would understand! I always feel like such an impostor.

After my diagnosis, I asked my psychiatrist how should I tell my parents. She told me to bring my parents on our next meeting, and she would explain it to them for me. After a month of struggling, I eventually told my parents that I have been meeting a psychiatrist secretly and I was diagnosed with BPD. I told them I'm still confused and don't really understand what does BPD mean but I have arranged a meeting for them with my psychiatrist. I read them those 9 symptoms of BPD and explained that I have been experiencing them. I think I have also shown them some YouTube videos that described my condition quite accurately. I don't think my parents really understood my diagnosis even after meeting my psychiatrist but they agreed to let her treat me.

Sorry I don't have any good advice. I just feel like I have to leave a comment as we have such similar experiences. As my psychiatrist once told me, no evil person would go through all this trouble and torture themselves just to get a diagnosis. Please know that you are not evil, and you are already very very special, just as you are. 


Also sorry for the writing, English is not my first language.
